keyChanges.title: Q2 Call: AI5 Volume Still 'Hopefully 2027'; Samsung/TSMC/Micron Named; AI6 Boast Unbacked
keyChanges.description: On Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, Musk reaffirmed that AI5 is expected in volume production 'hopefully next year' (2027), saying the chip design team 'exceeded expectations' — a design-quality compliment, not a production pull-forward. He publicly thanked Samsung and TSMC for major compute-capacity investments supporting Optimus (and robotaxi) silicon, and thanked Micron for a 'significant' multi-year memory allocation at 'reasonable' terms amid what he called 'pretty insane' memory prices (a 'hundred-year flood' / biggest price jump he has seen). Nikkei and TrendForce quote Musk claiming AI6 will be 'the best edge computing chip in the world' while development continues; no AI6 tape-out or production date was advanced beyond prior mid-2028 framing. Official Q2 shareholder deck quantifies Cortex training clusters (Cortex 1 >90 MW, Cortex 2 >115 MW in production; onsite Texas MW more than doubled in H1 2026) but contains no AI5 wafer starts, yield figures, or board-volume milestones. Reality check: Samsung foundry-side AI5 tape-out (July 13) already filed last week; volume AI5 remains H2 2027 / vehicle meaningful deployment 2028+; Cybercab and current fleets still ship on AI4; memory allocation is necessary insurance in a shortage, not proof of inference-chip ramp.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Named foundry/memory partners and 'design exceeded expectations' sound bullish, but AI5 volume date is unchanged at 2027, AI6 claim is unbacked marketing, and no new wafer/yield/board metrics were disclosed.

positive_signals: Musk: AI5 chip design team 'exceeded expectations'; volume production 'hopefully next year' (2027) reiterated on official call
Samsung and TSMC explicitly credited for major compute investments tied to Optimus/robotaxi silicon scale-up

Cortex 1 >90 MW and Cortex 2 >115 MW both in production; Tesla onsite Texas training compute (MW) more than doubled in H1 2026 (Q2 shareholder update)
Dual-source AI5 path (Samsung Taylor 2nm + TSMC) still intact after July 13 foundry tape-out context
negative_signals: AI5 volume still 2027 — no acceleration vs prior mid/late-2027 guidance; nearly ~2 years behind original timelines
No disclosed AI5 wafer starts, yield %, engineering-sample qualification status, or completed board counts toward the 'hundreds of thousands of boards' line-switchover bar
AI6 'best edge chip in the world' is aspirational PR with no new tape-out/date; AI6 previously slipped toward mid-2028 on Samsung 2nm risk
Vehicles, Robotaxi Model Ys, and Cybercab still launching/shipping on AI4 (or AI4.x) — AI5 not in commercial hardware yet
Memory 'win' is defensive amid industry-wide DRAM shortage (Cook/Musk 'hundred-year flood'); does not prove inference-chip manufacturing readiness
Q2 deck's only AI Inference Compute paragraph focuses on early-stage Austin semiconductor fab (Terafab path) — foundry partners still carry near-term volume risk
Not a Tesla App / call summary: vehicle production also described as electronics/chip constrained alongside batteries — supply tightness, not abundance

key_metrics.actual: AI5 volume target still 2027; Cortex 1 >90 MW + Cortex 2 >115 MW training; no public AI5 unit production count
key_metrics.target: High-volume AI5 boards for vehicle line switchover mid/late 2027; AI6 thereafter
key_metrics.trajectory: Design milestones (April design tape-out; July Samsung foundry tape-out) progressing; manufacturing volume still ~12+ months out with no yield proof

keyChanges.title: Micron Multi-Year Memory Allocation Highlighted; AI Board BOM Still Supply-Risk Bound
keyChanges.description: Coverage of the July 22 earnings call (TrendForce 2026-07-23, Wccftech 2026-07-22, Bloomberg headline) centers on Musk thanking Micron for making 'room for Tesla in the years to come' with significant memory allocation at non-panic pricing. TrendForce frames this against Micron's Strategic Customer Agreements (3–5 year price+volume locks; 16 SCAs covering ~20% DRAM / ~1/3 NAND at Micron's prior call) and notes auto OEMs already face multi-billion DRAM inflation. For Tesla AI computers, high unified memory (Electronics Weekly's July 13 A15/AI5 writeup cited up to 144GB-class configs in secondary coverage — treat as unverified spec chatter) makes DRAM a first-class BOM risk alongside Samsung/TSMC logic wafers. Positive for de-risking Optimus/Robotaxi board builds if allocation is real; critical caveat: allocation ≠ free capacity, terms are undisclosed, and logic foundry 2nm yield at Taylor remains the gating item for AI5 volume — memory thanks do not move the AI5 production clock.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Multiple outlets quote Musk on Micron allocation, but contract size/price/duration are undisclosed and memory relief does not resolve 2nm AI5 manufacturing risk.

keyChanges.title: Q2 IR: battery pack capacity is the global vehicle bottleneck; 4680 ramp for Cybercab/Semi/MY
keyChanges.description: Tesla’s Q2 2026 Update (July 22) is the first IR-level admission this cycle that battery pack capacity is “the main limiting factor to near-term vehicle production volume increase” and “remains the limiting factor on ramping our vehicle production globally.” Management says it is “increasing production of 4680 cells to support production ramps of both Cybercab and Tesla Semi and increased production of Model Y,” alongside vehicle pack capacity work in Berlin, cathode materials and lithium refining in Texas, and LFP cells in Nevada for energy storage. The installed-capacity table is the hard data: Texas 4680 is listed at >40 GWh under “Production,” while Berlin 4680 still shows no capacity figure and status “Construction” — a stark contrast to May 12 “production start” / July 16 cell-line video PR that framed Berlin as already making cells. Footnotes restate that installed capacity ≠ current production rate. Teslarati and TechCrunch corroborate that Musk/letter language ties 4680 cell output to Cybercab and Semi scale, and that prior “volume production this year” framing for those programs was softened; Outlook only commits Semi to “production starting in 2026,” not volume. No yield %, scrap rate, cost/kWh, or actual GWh of 4680 cells shipped was disclosed. Cell Giga Challenge applications still ran through July 24, underscoring ongoing external solicitation for manufacturing fixes.

No yield %, scrap, cost/kWh, or actual GWh of 4680 cells produced/shipped disclosed with earnings

keyChanges.title: Tesla adds unsupervised Robotaxi in Orlando and Tampa — 7 metros, still tiny fleets
keyChanges.description: On July 21, 2026, Tesla Robotaxi officially added Orlando and Tampa, FL — 18 days after Miami — bringing live footprints to seven regions (Austin hybrid, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa unsupervised; Bay Area safety-monitor only). TeslaNorth, Teslarati, and TeslaOracle corroborate unsupervised Model Y operation with no cabin safety personnel. Geofences remain deliberately small: Orlando ~12–45 sq mi (corridor near Semoran/Lee Vista, not MCO airport); Tampa covers West Tampa, Tampa Heights, Hyde Park, downtown. Headline is geographic expansion; reality is logo-on-map growth. Electrek (corroboration only) estimates ~21 active unsupervised vehicles across Austin/Dallas/Tampa/Orlando, with Austin down from ~25 in late April to ~17. Spreading a ~20-car garage across more cities degrades availability without proving scale. Purpose-built Cybercab still not in paid commercial fleets.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Real unsupervised city adds in Florida, but geofences are pilot-sized and active fleet remains ~dozens after ~1 year — expansion of map dots, not network density.

Third and fourth Florida cities live only weeks after Miami — faster regional cadence
Live coverage now cited as seven major metro areas in Q2 shareholder materials

keyChanges.title: Cybercab: Giga Texas production + 125k capacity claim; Moravy says no more federal approvals needed
keyChanges.description: Q2 materials and TeslaNorth report Tesla began Cybercab production at Gigafactory Texas (pilot since Feb 2026; official production narrative in Q2), with installed annual capacity cited above 125,000 units (Basenor from earnings release). Campus employee rides and engineering road tests are underway; purpose-built units remain outside paid commercial Robotaxi fleets. On the earnings call, VP Vehicle Engineering Lars Moravy answered whether further federal regulatory changes are required for Cybercab ops with a flat 'Short answer, no' — Tesla argues FMVSS self-certification avoids NHTSA’s 2,500-unit AV exemption cap, and EPA Certificate of Conformity for MY2026 was already effective May 26, 2026. Separately, Tesla revealed factory-integrated Starlink V5 terminals in Cybercab (rear-window/roof package with GPS/5G) for persistent connectivity and passenger 4K streaming. Critical read: federal pathway clarity and capacity slides are necessary but not sufficient — state/city permits, unsupervised safety bar, and actual commercial Cybercab deployment remain open. Capacity ≠ vehicles in revenue service.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Production start, 125k capacity, federal self-cert claim, and Starlink integration are real product steps; commercial robotaxi still runs on Model Y and Cybercab is not yet a paid fleet vehicle.

keyChanges.title: Q2 Robotaxi data: 2.4M paid miles but QoQ flat; Musk blames safety, fleet still not scaling
keyChanges.description: Tesla’s Q2 2026 update and July 22 earnings call put official numbers on Robotaxi for the first time in months: 2.4 million cumulative paid miles (~900k added in Q2, roughly flat vs Q1), and Ashok Elluswamy’s claim of 0 notable incidents across 380,000+ unsupervised miles with weekly miles growing double-digits. Musk told investors the constraint is not ambition but zero-injury risk — any harm becomes global headlines and regulatory clampdown. Analyst Colin Langan pressed why Tesla adds cities with dozens of vehicles instead of hundreds; Elluswamy said multi-city expansion is to prove a general stack, not to densify one market. Electrek’s differencing of Tesla’s own cumulative chart (Tier 2 corroboration) shows the ramp stalled: Q2 ≈ Q1 paid miles, April front-loaded (~500k) then May–June slowed (~200k/mo), and active unsupervised fleet still ~21 cars. After ~1 year of paid service, this is failed commercial scaling dressed as a safety narrative — cumulative miles always go up; utilization and fleet size do not.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Official 2.4M paid miles and clean unsupervised incident claim are real, but QoQ paid-mile adds are flat, fleet remains dozens, and Musk’s safety framing does not reverse year-long failure to scale utilization.

keyChanges.title: NHTSA EA26002 escalates: demands Tesla 'Radar Saves Us' internal docs and marketing justification
keyChanges.description: NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation (Director Tanya Topka) sent Tesla a 24-part information request under Engineering Analysis EA26002 (low-visibility FSD crashes), dated July 2 and reported July 21, 2026. Request No. 4 specifically demands all communications, technical docs, test records, and underlying data tied to an internal Tesla document titled 'Radar Saves Us' that Tesla previously submitted during PE24031-01. ODI states the document appears relevant to degradation-detection design and Tesla's understanding of vision-only OEDR limits in the reduced-visibility conditions of nine countable crashes (including one fatality and one injury) across ~3.2 million FSD-capable US vehicles. Other IRs probe 15 marketing statements for overclaiming automation level, the 2024 'FSD Degraded' alert change from red to yellow with chime removed, 'Direct Photon-Count Capability,' Vision Failsafe Ranker, and internal regression metrics. Tesla response deadline: August 12, 2026; civil penalties up to ~$27,874/day for incomplete answers (capped near $139M). Critical framing: EA is the last step before close or recall push. An internal memo named 'Radar Saves Us' implies Tesla analyzed camera-only failure modes that match the crash pattern after removing radar in 2021 — elevating knowledge-of-defect risk. NHTSA EA26002 and Special Crash Investigation remain open; this is escalation of the probe already noted in prior weeks, not a new investigation.

Tesla has until August 12 to respond and can produce technical rebuttal
NTSB prelim on separate Katy crash previously attributed override to driver (software not primary cause in that case)

keyChanges.title: France rejects FSD Supervised: Transport Minister cites speeding and driver-monitoring gaps
keyChanges.description: On or around July 22, 2026, French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot publicly stated that France will not authorize Tesla Full Self-Driving (Supervised) 'as it currently stands,' saying 'the safety trade-offs are not yet sufficient.' Specific objections: (1) FSD can exceed posted limits to match traffic — Tabarot cited up to ~70 km/h in a 50 km/h zone (~40% over); (2) driver monitoring does not guarantee adequate attention in complex urban maneuvers (lane changes, intersections, roundabouts); (3) French guidelines still expect hands on the wheel. France is refusing to rubber-stamp Dutch RDW national homologation and wants a harmonized EU-wide framework; technical talks with Tesla, the Netherlands, and other member states continue, with a Ministry rep having visited NL data recently and ecosystem meetings planned for autumn. EU-wide mutual-recognition vote still needs 15 member states representing ≥65% of EU population; next potential vote flagged for October. Musk replied on X: 'Delaying the approval of FSD in France will cost lives.' Critical reality: France is a top-tier EU volume market. Consumer FSD Supervised remains live only in five small markets (NL/LT/EE/DK/BE). Germany, France, Italy, Spain, and UK still closed. Tesla's summer-2026 EU-wide mutual-recognition narrative has failed for major markets; France's public rejection plus Sweden's earlier speeding-based opposition raise the bar for October.

Tabarot said France 'supports these technologies' and is ready to engage if safety bar is met

Five smaller EU markets (NL/LT/EE/DK/BE) remain live with 50M+ km driven
negative_signals: Official rejection of current FSD Supervised by a major EU auto market's Transport Minister
Concrete safety defects cited: speeding up to ~40% over limit and insufficient urban driver attention

Summer 2026 EU-wide recognition target not delivered; next vote only October and needs 15 states / 65% population
Sweden already urged EU rejection over speeding; France adds a large-population no vote risk for October
Musk 'cost lives' response does not resolve regulatory technical objections

keyChanges.title: FSD v14 Lite goes public for HW3 (2026.20.6.10/.11); HW4 gets point-release v14.3.6 — still Supervised only
keyChanges.description: Tesla restarted and then publicly expanded FSD (Supervised) v14 Lite for HW3/AI3 vehicles with software 2026.20.6.10 (July 20–21), after Ashok Elluswamy said the updated Lite build was 'likely the version that goes to wide release.' NotATeslaApp and TeslaNorth report regular US/Canada HW3 owners beyond early access receiving the OTA; IR shareholder letter confirms v14 Lite delivery began for AI3 customers in the US and South Korea. Official notes: distilled HW4 v14 intelligence into HW3 (RL + offline models), parking/unparking/reversing, Arrival Options, Speed Profiles including SLOTH, optional brake-confirm, Self-Driving app, and streak tracking. Concurrently, 2026.20.6.11 ships FSD Supervised v14.3.6 for HW4 — release notes largely restate the v14.3.5 RL/vision-encoder/MLIR stack with TeslaFi showing ~1.5k cars / ~12% of tracked fleet mid-rollout. Critical reality: this is supervised feature parity and legacy-fleet catch-up, not autonomy progress. Lite is explicitly a distilled student model (slower decision-making than full HW4 v14); HW3 remains permanently capped below unsupervised FSD and is not expected to get v15. Consumer production ceiling is still the v14.3.x branch while robotaxi early-v15 work continues in parallel.

keyChanges.title: Ashok: Robotaxi fleet already running early FSD v15 builds — only ~40% of planned improvements, consumer still on v14
keyChanges.description: On the July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy confirmed that the currently operating Robotaxi fleet (retrofitted HW4/AI4 Model Ys) is already running early versions of FSD v15 software. He said Tesla targeted seven major improvement tracks over v14 for v15, developed in parallel, and that early fleet builds already contain about 40% of those planned improvements with internal benchmarks hitting their objectives. As work completes, he claimed the car will be 'ridiculously safe and capable.' Critical reality: this is the first official confirmation that any public-road vehicles run v15, ending weeks of 'no public v15 builds' silence — but it is fleet-only, incomplete (~60% of tracks still unfinished), and not a consumer OTA. Production Supervised FSD for owners remains on the v14.3.x branch (v14.3.6 rolling with 2026.20.6.11). Public consumer v15 is still framed as later this year or early next year — the same delayed end-2026/early-2027 window previously cited as the robotaxi-scale architectural blocker. Early v15 on a small unsupervised fleet is validation progress, not the 10B-parameter consumer ship event investors have been waiting for.

keyChanges.title: Q2 IR: 1.48M paid FSD customers (+200k QoQ, +56% YoY); 55% North America delivery attach
keyChanges.description: Tesla’s Q2 2026 shareholder update and earnings call disclosed active paid FSD customers reached 1.48 million globally (up from 1.28M in Q1 and 0.95M in Q2 2025 — +56% YoY), with record North America attach of over 55% of new deliveries including an FSD subscription at delivery. Mix: ~55% upfront purchases / ~45% subscriptions; Tesla says future monetization growth will skew to subscriptions after removing purchase option in most markets. Cumulative FSD (Supervised) miles approaching 12 billion (consistent with prior-week community 12B milestone). Critical framing: this is strong commercial demand for Supervised L2 software and validates FSD as a demand driver (Musk: buyers want 'FSD with a car attached'), but it is not a software capability milestone. The product customers are buying remains attention-required Supervised FSD on v14.x; the Musk compensation-plan 10M active FSD subscriber target is still ~6.8M away (~15% of goal). Subscription growth can accelerate without shipping unsupervised v15.

keyChanges.title: Optimus hiring pulse continues — manufacturing/test/production roles, but still no fill-rate or headcount proof

keyChanges.title: Q2 earnings: Musk confirms Optimus has no supply chain and a 'flat and long' ramp
keyChanges.description: On Tesla's July 22, 2026 Q2 earnings call and in the Q2 shareholder update, management finally answered the production-ramp questions investors had queued — and the answers lowered expectations. Official letter language: Fremont Model S/X lines are decommissioned; Tesla is 'installing the first-generation lines for Optimus, where we expect to start production soon' / 'anticipated production later this year.' Initial builds 'will be used in our Optimus Academy for training data collection and further functionality development.' Giga Texas Optimus site development is 'in full swing' but still construction, not output. Musk on the call: Optimus is 'the hardest product to scale manufacturing that we've ever made at Tesla because everything on the robot is new'; 'with Optimus, there is no supply chain' so Tesla must build it from scratch or insource; the manufacturing S-curve's 'initial portion… will be quite flat and long'; reliability fear framed as a 70 kg robot that can 'flop over' if it goes haywire. He still called Optimus Tesla's 'biggest product ever' and floated aspirational Optimus 4 at Austin targeting '10 million units a year versus 1 million units a year of Optimus 3' — with heavy caveats. Capex is >$25B for the year; Q2 free cash flow was −$1.09B on $5.8B capex as AI/robotics spend accelerated. Stock fell ~12–14.5% the next day (~$140B market cap), with coverage citing limited new Optimus milestones. Reality: late-July/August full-scale start window is not confirmed as met; letter still says 'soon'/'later this year'; zero disclosed unit counts, yield, takt time, factory deployment tasks, 2027 external sales volume, or pricing; all near-term robots remain internal Academy training units. Competitors (Agility Digit) already generate warehouse revenue while Tesla remains pre-revenue on Optimus.

keyChanges.title: Q2 earnings: record $28.2B revenue, but op margin collapses to 1.4% and FCF goes negative
keyChanges.description: Tesla reported Q2 2026 financials on July 22 after the already-known 480,126 delivery / 451,758 production print. Revenue hit a record $28.236B (+26% YoY, beat ~$26.4–27.6B Street), and TTM revenue crossed $100B for the first time. The P&L underneath is ugly: non-GAAP EPS $0.33 vs ~$0.53 expected (miss of ~$0.20), operating income $398M (−57% YoY), operating margin 1.4% (vs 4.1% YoY and vs ~5.4% pre-earnings Street consensus), free cash flow −$1.092B on CapEx of $5.789B (+142% YoY). Gross margin held relatively better at 16.8% (−41 bps YoY), so the damage was opex and mix, not just discounting. Regulatory credit revenue collapsed to $146M (−67% YoY from $439M), removing near-pure profit after the federal EV credit / CAFE penalty market evaporated. GAAP net income $1.114B (−5% YoY) was propped by ~$590M other income (bitcoin MTM / FX). Management framed CapEx run-rate above $25B for full-year 2026 as deliberate AI/robotics/autonomy spend. Market verdict: TSLA fell ~14.5% on July 23 to ~$320, erasing >$140B market value — one of the steeper single-day drops in years. Critical read: the Q2 delivery beat did not translate into a healthy auto quarter. Volume was inventory-fed (prod 28k below del), ASP pressure + AI opex + dead credit line crushed operating leverage. Cash burn better than the −$3.25B Street worst-case, but 1.4% op margin is incompatible with a re-rating of the car business.

keyChanges.title: TSLA drops ~14.5% post-earnings as Street digests profit miss and $25B+ CapEx path
keyChanges.description: On July 23, the first full session after the Q2 report, Tesla shares fell approximately 14.5%, closing near $320 after opening around $374, wiping out more than $140B in market value on heavy volume. The move ranks among Tesla's steeper single-day percentage declines in years. The catalyst was not the already-known delivery beat but the combination of a large EPS miss ($0.33 vs ~$0.53), 1.4% operating margin, negative free cash flow, and management's willingness to run CapEx above $25B for 2026 with limited new concrete Robotaxi/Optimus commercial milestones on the call. Pre-earnings IR consensus had already baked in thin margins and negative FCF; the actual 1.4% op margin undershot even that cautious setup. Critical read: the market is no longer willing to re-rate the auto business on volume alone while AI/robotics spend suppresses near-term profitability. Delivery strength is being treated as a one-quarter inventory/demand bounce, not proof of durable high-margin auto growth.

keyChanges.title: Gov. Abbott Submits Positive JETI Determinations for SpaceX Terafab; Deal Still Needs Formal Signing
keyChanges.description: On July 21, 2026, KBTX confirmed with the Texas Comptroller’s office that Governor Greg Abbott and both Grimes County school districts (Iola ISD and Anderson-Shiro CISD) have submitted positive determinations on all eight SpaceX Terafab JETI school-property-tax agreements—clearing the discretionary political gates that had left the project in limbo after the July 15 statutory decision deadline. Official verification letters were not yet posted to the Comptroller’s website at the time of reporting, and the Governor’s office did not respond to KBTX comment requests. With positive determinations from all three required parties, the remaining step is formal three-party execution of the agreements and filing with the Comptroller before Phase 1 construction can begin under the JETI framework. SpaceX still targets Phase 1 construction before year-end 2026 on the ~22,000-acre Grimes County site near Gibbons Creek; building permits and groundwater applications were not on file as of prior mid-June document reporting. Political/tax track advanced, but dirt has not moved and the abatements remain unsigned.

keyChanges.title: Tesla Q2 Update: Early-Stage Austin Semiconductor Fab Construction and Equipment Procurement Underway
keyChanges.description: In its Q2 2026 shareholder update (released with July 22 earnings), Tesla stated it is making progress on construction and equipment procurement for a semiconductor fab in Austin, while labeling the project 'still in its early stages' and critical for long-term logic/memory supply. Highlights also said site selection, preparation, construction, and equipment procurement progressed in the quarter for solar and semiconductor manufacturing, with multi-year semiconductor manufacturing capacity build-out 'underway.' On the earnings call, Musk called Terafab an 'amazing initiative' and a 'high-risk, high-payoff bet on AI chips,' confirmed equipment orders for a development fab in Austin, and described an integrated stack (lithography mask production, logic, memory, packaging, and chip testing under one roof) for faster iteration—framing it as necessary to scale Optimus. Capex more than doubled to $5.8B in Q2 with free cash flow of negative $1.1B and full-year spend guided above $25B. This is an early development-fab signal in Austin, not proof of Grimes County megafab groundbreaking or volume wafer production; dual tracks (Tesla Austin development fab vs. SpaceX Grimes JETI megasite) remain only partially closed politically and still early operationally.
